texts: bad: "is not a substitute for X" has no shape the translator can build — the "for sea-water" complement ends up hanging off the bare word "substitute" rather than off salt, and the whole claim (the "in distillation" restriction included) gets buried inside a preposition atom, so nothing about salt is queryable and "sea-water" loses its link to water. Say it with a plain verb and a modal instead, which has a licensed kind-level form and a licensed slot for the domain restriction: "In distillation, salt cannot replace sea-water."
good. the store, the drawing, the deep ebb it draws from and the ebb's position at the mouth are all covered, with the mouth linked to the harbor as a part.
